{
  "findings": [

      "line": 1,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Accidental submodule/gitlink added to repository root",
      "body": "The PR adds a file named `sentry-repo` containing a Git subproject commit pointer. This looks like an accidental embedded repository/submodule rather than an intentional source change. There is no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry or documented reason for it, and it can break clones, CI checkouts, and tooling that does not expect an embedded repository at the repo root. It should be removed from the PR."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py",
      "line": 220,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Upsampling decision uses the original dataset/request instead of the query actually executed",
      "body": "`_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, and may later execute a modified query such as a dashboard-split query (`... AND !event.type:transaction` or `... AND event.type:transaction`). However the upsampling eligibility check is computed from the outer `dataset` and the original HTTP request only: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)`. It does not consider the actual `scoped_dataset` or the final `query` being executed. This can cause the `count()` rewrite to be applied to a transaction-like query, or skipped for an error-only split query, leading to incorrect counts or query failures. The eligibility check should be based on the actual dataset and query passed to the query executor."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py",
      "line": 137,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Substring check for `event.type:error` can misclassify discover queries",
      "body": "`_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the raw query string contains the substring `event.type:error`. This is unsafe for Sentry search syntax: it matches negated queries such as `!event.type:error`, compound queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and text inside quoted values. For the discover dataset this enables `upsampled_count()` for mixed or non-error event queries, where `sample_weight` may be missing, zero, or inapplicable, producing silently incorrect counts. The check needs to parse/understand the query rather than using a raw substring match."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py",
      "line": 1046,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "`upsampled_count` assumes valid integral `sample_weight` values",
      "body": "The new `upsampled_count` aggregate is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. This has two data-correctness risks: (1) if any event in an allowlisted project has a NULL/missing/zero `sample_weight`, the contribution can be dropped or become zero even though the event exists; (2) if `sample_weight` can be fractional, `toInt64` truncates the summed result and biases counts downward. Project-level allowlisting does not by itself guarantee every event has a valid integral weight. Consider using an explicit fallback such as `coalesce(sample_weight, 1)` and avoiding lossy integer casting unless weights are guaranteed integral."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py",
      "line": 38,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Eligibility cache can serve stale upsampling decisions and invalidation is not wired",
      "body": "`is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches project allowlist eligibility for 60 seconds keyed by organization and project set. If the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option changes during that window, especially when a project is removed from the allowlist, queries can continue to use upsampled counts incorrectly. The provided `invalidate_upsampling_cache` helper is not called from anywhere, and it only invalidates one exact project-set key rather than all affected keys. This creates a data-integrity window after configuration changes. Include a config/version token in the cache key or wire up broader invalidation."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py",
      "line": 27,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Cache key construction sorts and hashes all project IDs on every call",
      "body": "The cache key is built with `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))` before checking whether the dataset/query is even eligible for upsampling. For organizations with many projects, this adds sorting and hashing overhead to every events-stats request, including datasets where upsampling is never applied. A cheaper early-out for non-applicable datasets, or a more efficient stable key, would avoid undermining the stated performance optimization."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py",
      "line": 3610,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Endpoint tests do not exercise the explicit `errors` dataset path",
      "body": "The upsampling helper unconditionally applies for the `errors` dataset, but the added endpoint tests only use the default/discover path and one explicit `dataset=discover` case. There is no test with `dataset=errors`, so the branch where the rewrite is always enabled for the errors dataset is not covered. This is important because the new SnQL function was added in the discover dataset configuration and the errors-dataset behavior may differ."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Accidental submodule/gitlink added to repository root
findings.body: The PR adds a file named `sentry-repo` containing a Git subproject commit pointer. This looks like an accidental embedded repository/submodule rather than an intentional source change. There is no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry or documented reason for it, and it can break clones, CI checkouts, and tooling that does not expect an embedded repository at the repo root. It should be removed from the PR.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses the original dataset/request instead of the query actually executed
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, and may later execute a modified query such as a dashboard-split query (`... AND !event.type:transaction` or `... AND event.type:transaction`). However the upsampling eligibility check is computed from the outer `dataset` and the original HTTP request only: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)`. It does not consider the actual `scoped_dataset` or the final `query` being executed. This can cause the `count()` rewrite to be applied to a transaction-like query, or skipped for an error-only split query, leading to incorrect counts or query failures. The eligibility check should be based on the actual dataset and query passed to the query executor.

findings.title: Substring check for `event.type:error` can misclassify discover queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the raw query string contains the substring `event.type:error`. This is unsafe for Sentry search syntax: it matches negated queries such as `!event.type:error`, compound queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and text inside quoted values. For the discover dataset this enables `upsampled_count()` for mixed or non-error event queries, where `sample_weight` may be missing, zero, or inapplicable, producing silently incorrect counts. The check needs to parse/understand the query rather than using a raw substring match.

findings.title: `upsampled_count` assumes valid integral `sample_weight` values
findings.body: The new `upsampled_count` aggregate is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. This has two data-correctness risks: (1) if any event in an allowlisted project has a NULL/missing/zero `sample_weight`, the contribution can be dropped or become zero even though the event exists; (2) if `sample_weight` can be fractional, `toInt64` truncates the summed result and biases counts downward. Project-level allowlisting does not by itself guarantee every event has a valid integral weight. Consider using an explicit fallback such as `coalesce(sample_weight, 1)` and avoiding lossy integer casting unless weights are guaranteed integral.

findings.title: Eligibility cache can serve stale upsampling decisions and invalidation is not wired
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches project allowlist eligibility for 60 seconds keyed by organization and project set. If the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option changes during that window, especially when a project is removed from the allowlist, queries can continue to use upsampled counts incorrectly. The provided `invalidate_upsampling_cache` helper is not called from anywhere, and it only invalidates one exact project-set key rather than all affected keys. This creates a data-integrity window after configuration changes. Include a config/version token in the cache key or wire up broader invalidation.

findings.title: Cache key construction sorts and hashes all project IDs on every call
findings.body: The cache key is built with `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))` before checking whether the dataset/query is even eligible for upsampling. For organizations with many projects, this adds sorting and hashing overhead to every events-stats request, including datasets where upsampling is never applied. A cheaper early-out for non-applicable datasets, or a more efficient stable key, would avoid undermining the stated performance optimization.

findings.title: Endpoint tests do not exercise the explicit `errors` dataset path
findings.body: The upsampling helper unconditionally applies for the `errors` dataset, but the added endpoint tests only use the default/discover path and one explicit `dataset=discover` case. There is no test with `dataset=errors`, so the branch where the rewrite is always enabled for the errors dataset is not covered. This is important because the new SnQL function was added in the discover dataset configuration and the errors-dataset behavior may differ.
